name: HexagonPattern
description: A honeycomb of hexagon outlines that fills its parent, with an optional edge fade and a slow drift.

size.description: Hexagon radius (centre to corner) in pixels.

color.description: Colour of the pattern: any CSS colour or a token such as var(--rd-color-border-default).

fade.description: Fades the pattern out toward its edges.

animated.description: Drifts the pattern slowly, one tile per cycle. Off by default.

isStill.description: Stops the drift. Moving content should be stoppable.

requirements: Pure decoration: aria-hidden, never focusable, and pointer-events none so content on top stays usable
It is drawn with CSS only, so it needs no JavaScript and is safe in server HTML
Stands still for visitors who ask for less motion (prefers-reduced-motion), with isStill, and inside an rdm-still container
Drift is slow and never flashes (WCAG 2.2.2, 2.3.1)
Hidden in forced-colors (high contrast) mode so it never fights system colours
Keep text on top at 4.5:1 against the lines: use a low-contrast token for the pattern

use_when: A quiet honeycomb behind a hero, card or empty state
Giving a flat surface a little texture
avoid_when: Behind long text where the lines reduce legibility
As the only way to show a boundary or meaning
anti_patterns: A high-contrast colour that competes with the content
Animating several patterns on one screen
